title: Sell Mineral Rights in Meadowlands, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Meadowlands, PA | Washington County
metaDescription: Meadowlands, PA sits inside Washington County's most-drilled Marcellus corridor. We buy mineral rights directly, with a clear look at your deductions.
heroLead: There's a reason so many royalty owners in Meadowlands already know the word decimal interest, this stretch of Washington County has been one of the busiest Marcellus corridors in the state for over a decade.
intro: Meadowlands sits along the North Strabane and Cecil township line, an area operators have returned to again and again for infill drilling since the early Marcellus years. If you're a landowner here, or you inherited a fraction of a family tract, there's a decent chance your interest has been part of more than one drilling unit over the years.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Meadowlands directly, and because this is such an active corridor, we spend time making sure we understand the full production picture, not only a single well's numbers, before we make an offer.

sections.heading: One of Washington County's Busiest Corridors
paragraphs: The wells around Meadowlands have been re-stimulated, re-permitted, and added to over the years as operators worked through their acreage position in North Strabane and Cecil townships. That kind of sustained activity means royalty history here can span multiple units and multiple operators, which is worth untangling carefully rather than glancing at a single check.

This part of Washington County sits deep in the wet-gas window, so natural gas liquids make up a meaningful share of production value, and processing costs for those liquids show up as deductions before your royalty percentage is applied.

sections.heading: Tracking a Multi-Unit Interest
paragraphs: If your acreage has been pooled into more than one horizontal unit over time, your royalty statements may come from different pad names even though the underlying interest hasn't changed. We sort through that using Washington County Recorder of Deeds records and the operator's division order history to confirm exactly what you own and where it's producing.
This is more work than a single-unit review, but it's the only way to give you an offer that reflects the whole picture.

sections.heading: What the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act Covers
paragraphs: Pennsylvania law guarantees a one-eighth royalty floor, but it doesn't cap how much can be deducted above that floor for gathering, compression, and dehydration. If your Meadowlands-area check has shrunk more than you expected, that's usually a lease-language question, and we'll help you understand where yours stands before discussing a purchase.

faqs.question: My royalty checks come from different well names over the years. Why?
faqs.answer: Active corridors like Meadowlands often see acreage pooled into successive units as operators develop their position. Different pad names don't mean your underlying interest changed, just which unit it's currently allocated to.

faqs.question: Does more drilling activity mean a higher offer?
faqs.answer: Generally sustained activity is a positive factor, but the real driver is your specific decimal interest and recent production, not the overall level of activity in the area.

faqs.question: What documents should I gather before contacting you?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease you or a predecessor signed, and your most recent division order or royalty statements are the most useful starting point.
